description: IMPACT Initiatives, through its REACH Initiative, published a rapid experimental radar-based damage proxy for the earthquakes of 24 June 2026 in Venezuela. It compares Sentinel-1 backscatter amplitudes from a pre-event annual baseline with two post-event acquisitions of 25 June 2026 as a z-score anomaly, masks the result to built-up areas with the GHSL built-surface product, and flags an Overture Maps building footprint as likely damaged when at least half of it overlaps the proxy. The product estimates 81,437 likely damaged buildings, and it also delivers the full analysed area. Coverage: the broader impacted area of the June 2026 earthquakes in Venezuela. Access: GeoPackage, zipped Shapefile and GeoJSON files on HDX. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: the provider states that the product is not triangulated or validated, that backscatter anomalies also respond to building density, debris, moisture, vegetation, topography and sensor geometry, and that it cannot say whether an individual building is damaged, destroyed or safe to return to. Simulation uses are rapid screening and prioritisation of field assessment, and a comparison layer when testing earthquake damage models against other remote assessments of the same event. Related records: the Conflict Ecology Sentinel-1 coherence product and the DISHA building damage analysis for the same earthquake.
